Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

important adjective

also it matters, it is important, importance

classical

Cic. Att. 11.22.2: illud meā magnī interest tē ut videam
Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre
Traupman 332

magnī interest

impersonal verb (intersum); to whom, meā, tuā or a genitive; how much, magnī, plūris, maximē, nihil

it is important, it matters a great deal

Latin says “X is important” as “X matters”: the thing that matters is the subject, as a clause (infinitive, ut, or a question) or a neuter pronoun; nihil interest, “it makes no difference”. Traupman gives magnus for the adjective and id magnī aestimāre, “to consider it important” (p. 332).

Examples

  • illud meā magnī interest tē ut videam

    it matters a great deal to me to see youCic. Att. 11.22.2

  • tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre

    it matters above all, to you and to me, that you get wellCic. Fam. 16.4.4

  • quōmodo fābula, sīc vīta: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert

    life is like a play: what matters is not how long it runs, but how well it is actedSen. Ep. 77.20

Other words

  • magnī rēfert — it is important, it matters

    impersonal verb, built like interest · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 77.20; Phaedr. 1.15: quid rēfert meā cui serviam, “what does it matter to me whom I serve”

    Frequent in comedy, rare in Cicero, who says interest (Lewis & Short). Quid rēfert? “What does it matter?”

  • magnī mōmentī — of great importance (of a thing)

    genitive of quality: rēs magnī mōmentī · also used · classical · Tac. H. 3.8; Liv. 10.16.5 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Vatin. 19: maximī mōmentī et ponderis (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. important

  • gravis, grave — weighty, important, serious

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.103: cum gravibus sēriīsque rēbus satis fēcerimus; M-O s.v. important

  • amplus, ampla, amplum — of a person: important, eminent

    also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 83 (Lewis & Short)

  • mōmentōsus, mōmentōsa, mōmentōsum — important

    avoid · modern · M-O s.v. important (marked as a modern word; Trappen 1843)

    Its only ancient use (Ps.-Quint. Decl. 13.12) means “momentary, quick”; magnī mōmentī says “important” classically.

SourcesLewis & Short: intersum · Lewis & Short: refert · Lewis & Short: momentum · Lewis & Short: gravis · Lewis & Short: magnus · Lewis & Short: amplus · Lewis & Short: momentosus
